name: MIMIC-III: Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III
description: MIMIC-III is a widely celebrated, freely accessible clinical database developed by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC), published in Nature Scientific Data. Spanning over a decade of critical care admissions between 2001 and 2012, MIMIC-III covers 46,520 distinct intensive care unit (ICU) patients across 58,976 hospital admissions. It integrates electronic health records from both CareVue and MetaVision ICU clinical information systems across 26 relational tables documenting patient demographics, continuous hourly physiological vital sign measurements, comprehensive laboratory blood chemistry and microbiological cultures, therapeutic medication administrations, nursing notes, and ICD-9 billing diagnoses. Crucially, MIMIC-III includes an integrated NOTEEVENTS table containing over 2 million de-identified free-text clinical notes, making it a foundational benchmark for clinical NLP, automated ICD coding, mortality prediction, and sepsis detection. Users should note that while MIMIC-IV supersedes MIMIC-III for contemporary MetaVision data (2008–2019), MIMIC-III remains a distinct historical benchmark capturing CareVue system data (2001–2008) and embedded clinical text notes.
